name: Jinja
comment: Hand-written for this extension; nothing vendored. Deliberately does NOT paint tags. A grammar hardcodes the delimiters, and a template's real delimiters can come from a `#jinja2:` header or from the `template:` task that renders it — so painting `{% %}` means confidently colouring literal output as a tag on exactly the files the server gets right. `textDocument/semanticTokens` paints tags instead, from the parser, and a semantic token overrides a grammar scope only where it provides one: silence cannot un-paint, so the grammar must not guess in the first place. What is left here is the part that is true regardless of delimiters.

interpolation-fallback.comment: The one shape worth keeping: `{{ … }}` with the default delimiters, painted only as a neutral punctuation scope so a template still reads as structured before the server answers. It names no keyword and no variable, so when the tokens arrive they refine rather than contradict, and on a file whose delimiters are overridden the worst case is a faint bracket rather than a word coloured as a tag.
interpolation-fallback.name: punctuation.definition.template-expression.jinja
